sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Grenoble prices its on-street parking in three zones and is stepping up enforcement. As of the city page updated on 27 August 2026, paid parking runs Monday to Saturday: the green zone costs 2 euros for one hour and 10.50 euros for eight hours, the orange and violet zones 3 euros for one hour, and the post-parking charge is 35 euros, or 135 euros for very obstructive parking [0]. Tariffs rose for all durations from 1 March 2022, when the first minutes stopped being free and the Jean-Macé district near the station became paid [16]. The city says it counts 35,500 parking spaces, of which 13,500 are paid, 18,900 free and 3,100 reserved, and local press reports that it is working to reduce the share of free parking, for example in Berriat, Europole and Île Verte [15]. Two cars with plate-reading cameras began checking paid zones on 5 October 2026 to speed up turnover, and an agent still issues each fine [1][2]. The city moved to the EasyPark app on 6 October 2025 and is replacing its 850 meters with card-accepting ones [14]. A resident ticket costs 12 euros a month, 9 a week or 3 a day, but because of the low-emission zone no resident right can be issued to holders of an unclassified or Crit'Air 3 to 5 light commercial or heavy goods vehicle [3]. On 2 July 2026 the Métropole extended the no-fine period of the zone by a year, to 30 June 2027 [4].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The main change is in who runs the public garages. Since 1 April 2019 the Métropole's 21 car parks, with 7,752 spaces, had been run by a joint venture called Park Grenoble Alpes Métropole, in which Effia held half and the Métropole the other half plus one share [7]. ParkGAM's own home page says that since 1 April 2026 the Métropole has entrusted their management to a public limited company with 100% public capital [6]. The Métropole now lists 22 public car parks with about 8,000 spaces, run by ParkGAM except Chavant, which Q-Park operates; seven are subscription-only and subscribers whose vehicle weighs over 1.5 tonnes pay a surcharge [9]. ParkGAM's Presqu'île page lists the surcharge thresholds as 1,550 kg for combustion vehicles and 1,800 kg for electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles; we did not find the date it was introduced [10].

Technology and charging are the other changes. ParkGAM promotes an app in its garages that opens barriers by plate recognition and debits payment the following month, without saying in which car parks [13]. Gares-Europole has 66 EV charging stations and Chavant 20 [11][12]. We found no source on new garages or on changes to the park-and-ride sites, of which the regional transport portal lists 22 in the Métropole and 45 across the wider area, with over 5,000 spaces [17].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Prices in the garages are close to the on-street ones. Presqu'île charges 2.40 euros for one hour and 29 euros for 24 hours, with half price from 19:00 to 08:00 [10]; Gares-Europole 2.40 euros an hour and 33 euros for 24 hours with a 39-euro weekend package [11]; and Q-Park's Chavant 2.30 euros an hour, 16 euros for six hours and 29 euros for 24 hours [12].

Our data cover 17 car parks from the national access-point feed. Thirteen of them, with 5,196 spaces, have at least a week of readings, starting between 24 September and 14 October 2026; the rest have only three days and are not used here. Occupancy averaged about 50% on weekdays and 42% at weekends, weighted by spaces. The busiest is Notre-Dame – Musée (851 spaces), which averaged 81% on weekdays and 66% at weekends and reached 96% on a Thursday evening. Parc Mistral – Mairie (400) averaged 62%, Catane (492) 58% on weekdays and 43% at weekends, and Estacade (581) 59%. The Chavant garage run by Q-Park (394 in our feed, 385 stated by Q-Park) is much quieter at 28% on both weekdays and weekends, and Saint-Bruno (120) averaged 8%. Several garages are noticeably less full at weekends, for example the Esplanade car park (128), which averaged 30% on weekdays and 10% at weekends. These are one to four weeks of data and should be read as a first picture.
